newsitem.title: USA: Great Western rescinds stock repurchase plan.
newsitem.headline: Great Western rescinds stock repurchase plan.

text.p: Great Western Financial Corp. said Wednesday it was ending its stock repurchase plan in connection with the California thrift's pending $6.6 billion merger with Washington Mutual Inc.
A Great Western spokesman said the move was "routine" and would ensure that the merger qualified as a pooling of interests.
Great Western continued to reject rival suitor H.F. Ahmanson & Co. even after the company on Monday raised the stakes in the takeover battle to about $7 billion.
Ahmanson, the nation's biggest savings and loan, had previously offered $6.1 billion for Great Western, but Washington Mutual made its higher bid -- which Great Western accepted -- on March 6.

Ahmanson stock climbed 62.5 cents to $39.625 and Great Western, based in Chatsworth, Calif., rose 37.5 cents to $44.375, both on the New York Stock Exchange. Washington Mutual was unchanged at $50.50 on Nasdaq.
